Title: Green Planning
Body: While out on the campaign trail, a hippie in a tie-dyed shirt approaches and asks what you will do to help create a more sustainable environment.
Narrative 1: I told a hippie that I will be fully committed to improving waste management if elected into office. I explained that the emphasis would be on reducing, reusing, and recycling to minimize landfill waste.
Narrative 2: I told a hippie that if I got elected into office, I would be fully committed to decreasing our dependence on coal, petroleum, and natural gas.
Narrative 3: I told a hippie that if I got elected into office, I would be fully committed to creating a policy that will protect our diverse ecosystems.
Narrative 4: I told a hippie that if I got elected into office, I would be fully committed to making environmental sustainability a more critical component of the educational curriculum. I added that it all starts with the youth, who are tomorrow's leaders.

Narrative 2: I told my opponent <he/she> was inappropriate and rude for calling me <insult> during our political debate. Then I continued to respond to a question about education that I had been answering, before being so rudely interrupted.

Choice 4: Call <him/her> a clown, then carry on

Narrative 4: I took a bribe from an oil lobbyist after learning that a campaign assistant did the same thing. To avoid detection, I had the money deposited into a dummy account.

Title: Deadly Donors
Body: A campaign assistant just emailed you a video showing <opponent> accepting illegal campaign donations from an executive representing a weapons corporation.

Title: Liquid Courage
Body: While waiting backstage, a campaign volunteer notices that you're feeling nervous about the speech you'll soon make in front of a very large audience. He pulls out a flask and asks you if you need a swig.
Narrative 1: I finished off a campaign volunteer's flask of whiskey before making a speech in front of a very large group. It went terribly wrong, with videos of my slurred speech going viral around the world.
Narrative 2: I took a small drink from a campaign volunteer's flask of whiskey before making a speech to a large group. I was a bit more buzzed than I anticipated and slipped up a few times, but the crowd didn't seem to notice.
Narrative 3: I politely declined when a campaign volunteer offered me a drink of whiskey from his flask. I explained that I was nervous about speaking in front of a massive crowd, but facing my fears will only make me a stronger person.
Narrative 4: I fired an intern for offering me whiskey before going on stage to speak in front of a massive audience.

Narrative 4: I avoided addressing economic issues after learning that voters in my <jurisdiction> were concerned about the state of the economy.

Title: Equal Opportunity
Body: During a heated debate, the moderator asks how you plan to ensure equality for all people in the <jurisdiction> if you become the next <political-office>.
Narrative 1: In a heated debate, I informed the public that I planned to focus on human rights if I got elected as the next <political-office>. I then reminded everyone that we, as humans, are all in this together.
Narrative 2: In a heated debate, I informed the public that I planned to focus on women's rights if I got elected as the next <political-office>. I added that it hurts all genders when we don't have gender equality.

Narrative 4: I told a reporter that equality for all people is essential, but if I got elected to be the next <political-office>, my bigger focus would be to ensure that the <jurisdiction> had a strong economy.

Title: Pets & Punishment
Body: During a press conference, a woman who appears to be a crazy cat lady asks how you will address animal cruelty issues if you become <political-office>.
Narrative 1: I told a cat lady that if I got elected to be the next <political-office>, my plan would be to make animal cruelty a crime punishable by death.
Choice 2: Make it a felony with a 10-year sentence

Choice 4: I'm more concerned about the economy
Narrative 4: I told a cat lady that if I got elected to be the next <political-office>, I would be more concerned with improving the economy than meddling with animal rights laws.

Title: State Focused
Body: In American politics, not all states are equal when it comes to electoral votes. With time running out, you must decide which state to focus your campaigning efforts on the most.
Narrative 1: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts on California's 55 electoral votes, the most of any state. I also wined and dined with Hollywood celebrities.
Narrative 2: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts on the 38 electoral votes deep in the heart of Texas.
Narrative 3: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts in Florida, where I could win the hearts of the retirees while securing the state's 29 electoral votes.
Narrative 4: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts in New York, knowing that if I was the big shot in the Big Apple that I could get the state's 29 electoral votes.
Narrative 5: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts in Colorado because I wanted to get the support of an environmentally conscious state, despite it only having nine electoral votes.
Narrative 6: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts in Hawaii so I could relax and enjoy some sun, even though they only have four electoral votes.
Narrative 7: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts in Alaska so that Americans would see how much I loved the great outdoors, despite it only having three electoral votes.
Narrative 8: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts in Alabama because I wanted to get better acquainted with the fine folk of the south, and I also wanted the state's nine electoral votes.
Narrative 9: With time running out, I focused my campaigning efforts in Washington DC because I wanted to make an impression in the nation's capital despite it only having three electoral votes.

Narrative 1: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, it would be to give every citizen a paid vacation.
Narrative 2: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, it would be to ban the sale and possession of assault rifles.
Narrative 3: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, I would make all public universities free to all students.
Choice 4: Felony for not using turn signal
Narrative 4: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, I would make it a felony to turn while driving without using a turn signal.
Narrative 5: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, I would outlaw black licorice.
Narrative 6: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, I would outlaw twerking.
Choice 7: Fine for chewing with mouth open
Narrative 7: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, I would make it a fineable offense to chew food with your mouth open.
Narrative 8: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, I would make cold calls a felony.
Narrative 9: I told a reporter that if I could only enact one law in the United States, I would legalize marijuana.

Title: More My Style
Body: While speaking before a large group on a college campus, a student asks you, if elected, what change you would most like to see at the White House.
Narrative 1: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would paint the White House pink.
Narrative 2: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would have a statue of myself erected in the White House rose garden.
Narrative 3: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would install a state-of-the-art sound system in the White House.
Choice 4: Build a pool on the front lawn
Narrative 4: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would install a swimming pool on the front lawn of the White House.
Narrative 5: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would convert a portion of the White House West Wing into a video arcade.
Choice 6: Install a hot tub in the Oval Office
Narrative 6: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would install a hot tub in the Oval Office at the White House.
Narrative 7: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would convert a portion of the White House cafeteria into a fully functioning McDonalds.
Narrative 8: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would install an IMAX theater in the White House.
Choice 9: Install a zipline across the property
Narrative 9: I told a college student that if I got elected, I would install a zipline at the White House that spanned the entire property.

Title: Billboard Bully
Body: While driving down one of the most crowded highways in the <jurisdiction>, you're shocked to discover <opponent> has leased a massive roadside billboard and commissioned an artist to paint your face onto a snake's body for all passerby to see.
Narrative 1: I retaliated against <opponent-possessive> attempt to slander me on a billboard by commissioning my own slanderous billboard depicting <his/her> face on a naked mole rat.
Narrative 2: I paid a guy to paint over the billboard <opponent> put up featuring my head on a snake's body.
Narrative 3: I decided it was best to simply ignore the billboard <opponent> commissioned featuring my head on a snake's body. I wouldn't stoop to <his/her> level.
Narrative 4: I reported to law enforcement that <opponent> put up a billboard featuring my head on a snake's body. They told me there was nothing they could do because no laws were broken.

Title: In Other News
Body: A popular news station in your <jurisdiction> has invited you to appear on their weekend edition to discuss your views on current issues. However, your campaign staff is concerned because the station openly supports <opponent>.
Narrative 1: I appeared on the weekend edition of a popular news program even though I knew the station openly supported <opponent>. It went great.
Narrative 2: I ignored a news station's request to have me appear on their weekend edition because I knew they openly supported <opponent>.
Narrative 3: I called into a news station instead of appearing live just in case things got out of hand.

Title: Wrath on Blast
Body: Amid a momentous campaign rally buzzing with energy, a protester suddenly begins shrieking accusations at you through a bullhorn, garnering the attention of the jumbotron.
Narrative 1: I allowed an angry protester to vent her frustrations about me during a campaign rally. After hearing her out, I responded to each of her gripes, leaving her speechless.
Narrative 2: I ordered security to remove an angry protester from my campaign rally after she caused a huge distraction.
Narrative 3: I walked off stage amid a campaign rally after the production crew gave undue attention to a protester in the crowd who was shrieking ridiculous accusations through a bullhorn.
Narrative 4: An angry protester bullied me with accusations during a political rally, but I used my quick wit to get the crowd laughing at her so loudly, nobody could hear what she was saying.

Title: Rowdy Rival
Body: Moments before appearing on stage for a live debate, <opponent> pulls you aside to covertly expose a whiskey flask in <his/her> coat pocket and asks if you'd like to ease the nerves before showtime.
Narrative 1: Just before appearing on stage for a live debate, <opponent> offered me some whiskey from a flask that was hidden in <his/her> coat pocket, but it didn't help, I ended up feeling lightheaded and woozy during the debate.
Narrative 2: Just before appearing on stage for a live debate, <opponent> attempted to get me drunk on whiskey, but I politely declined <his/her> offer.
Narrative 3: I called security on <opponent> after <he/she> tried offering me some unknown substance before a live debate. I'm pretty sure <he/she> was trying to drug me!
Narrative 4: Just before appearing on stage for a live debate, <opponent> attempted to derail my mental acuity by offering me a shot of whiskey from a flask hidden in <his/her> coat pocket. I took the flask and threw it across the room, then walked on stage and dominated the debate.

Title: Class Tech
Body: Voters are asking if you become <political-office>, will you seize new technological opportunities in the classrooms or continue to do things the old fashioned way?
Narrative 1: I told voters that as <political-office>, I would ensure the <jurisdiction-possessive> classrooms would be filled with the most cutting edge technology available.
Narrative 2: I told voters that as <political-office>, I'd make sure the <jurisdiction-possessive> classrooms would continue to operate in the manner of previous generations using books made of paper.
Choice 3: Mixing the old with the new
Narrative 3: I told voters that as <political-office>, I'd make sure the <jurisdiction-possessive> classrooms received the benefits of new technology as well as old fashioned methods of teaching.

Title: Easy Access
Body: While on the campaign trail, a young girl in a wheelchair approaches you asking, if you get elected, what will you do to make public areas in your <jurisdiction> more easily accessible for those with disabilities.
Narrative 1: I told a young girl in a wheelchair about my plans to make the <jurisdiction> more accessible to those with disabilities.
Narrative 2: I admitted to a young girl in a wheelchair that I hadn't yet developed plans to make the <jurisdiction> more accessible to those with disabilities, but after talking with her, I'd start right away! She was happy.
Narrative 3: I told a young girl in a wheelchair that making the <jurisdiction> more accessible to those with disabilities was not my job.
Narrative 4: While on the campaign trail, a young girl in a wheelchair approached me, asking about improved wheelchair accessibility, but I just ignored her.

Title: Manager Madness
Body: You've just received notification that your campaign manager no longer believes in your vision for running the <jurisdiction> and has quit to join <opponent-possessive> team.
Narrative 1: I immediately hired a new campaign manager after my good-for-nothing campaign manager quit.
Narrative 2: When my good-for-nothing campaign manager quit, I decided we didn't need a manager.
Narrative 3: After my good-for-nothing campaign manager suddenly quit our team, I filed a lawsuit claiming breach of contract.
Narrative 4: After my good-for-nothing campaign manager left my team, I decided to promote a volunteer to the manager position.

Title: Blackmail
Body: You've just received a suspicious email from an anonymous source that includes detailed personal information regarding your sexuality. The sender says you must comply with their demands or lewd photos of you will be released to the public.
Narrative 1: To avoid potential controversy, I surrendered to the demands of a blackmail attempt launched by an anonymous source via email.
Narrative 2: I ignored a blackmail attempt launched by an anonymous source via email.
Narrative 3: I called the police and reported a blackmail attempt launched by an anonymous source via email.
Narrative 4: I was blackmailed by an anonymous source via email threatening to post suggestive photos of me online, but I subverted their nefarious endeavor by posting the photos myself.

Title: Debate Diva
Body: During a live debate, <opponent> looks at you with a snarky smile and asks, "Do you think the country really needs a diva in the highest office right now"?
Narrative 1: When <opponent> called me a diva during a live debate, I replied with a smile and wink saying, "it takes one to know one, honey." The crowd roared in laughter.
Narrative 2: During a live debate, <opponent> called me as a diva. It was beneath me to respond.
Narrative 3: I tried to throw some hands at <opponent> when <he/she> called me a diva during a live debate, but security stopped me just before landing the first blow.
Narrative 4: <opponent> made me cry during a live debate by saying I was a diva.

Title: Who Run The World
Body: During a live debate, <opponent> looks at you with a snarky smile and asks, "Do you think this country, in its current state, could fly without a man helping out in the cockpit"?
Narrative 1: I ridiculed <opponent> during a live debate when <he/she> suggested I couldn't run the country without a man helping me.
Narrative 2: I tried to throw some hands at <opponent> when <he/she> said I needed a man to help me run the country, but security intercepted just before I landed the first blow.
Narrative 3: During a live debate, <opponent> implied that I needed a man to help me run the country. It was beneath me to respond.
Narrative 4: <opponent> made me cry during a live debate by saying I couldn't run the country without a man helping me.

Title: Party Lover
Body: While on the campaign trail, you get an invite to a conservative social event that you know would be good for publicity, but makes you question whether bringing <lover> with you is a good idea or not.
Narrative 1: I decided to invite my lover to attend a conservative social with me. We got some stares, but ultimately I'm glad he was there.
Narrative 2: I decided to attend a conservative social without <lover>. I didn't think it was the right crowd for us.
Narrative 3: I decided I'd rather stay at home with <lover> than go to a conservative social event.
Narrative 4: I decided to take a female friend with me to a conservative social event.

Title: News Flash
Body: While being interviewed on one of the <jurisdiction-possessive> most popular news stations, the anchor asks, "what do you say to those who think you're inadequate to run the <jurisdiction> because of your sexuality"?
Narrative 1: I told all those haters, who thought I wouldn't make a good <political-office> because of my sexuality, that love is love, and love would help our <jurisdiction> grow.
Narrative 2: I told all those haters, who thought I wouldn't make a good <political-office> because of my sexuality, that they were morons living in a bygone era.
Narrative 3: I didn't respond to those people who thought I would be unfit to be <political-office> because of my sexuality. You can't teach common sense.
Narrative 4: I told all those who questioned my competence to be <political-office> because of my sexuality that I'd not only be the best <political-office> this <jurisdiction> had ever seen, but I'd also be the best dressed, as well.

Title: Tea Time
Body: You're about to host a special luncheon for a potential campaign donor who is very sophisticated, extremely wealthy, and adores a good cup of tea.
Narrative 1: I served English breakfast tea to a sophisticated potential campaign donor during a hosted luncheon, and she was so pleased with the meal we hooked her for a donation!
Narrative 2: I served chamomile tea to a sophisticated potential campaign donor during a hosted luncheon, but he ended up falling asleep throughout the entire meal, and didn't donate to my campaign!
Narrative 3: I served green tea to a sophisticated potential campaign donor during a hosted luncheon, and she was so pleased with the meal we hooked her for a donation!
Narrative 4: I served peppermint tea to a sophisticated potential campaign donor during a hosted luncheon, and she was so pleased with the meal we hooked her for a donation!

Title: Skip the Ads
Body: You've just discovered that <opponent> posted an ad campaign on Facebook that smears your political views with misinformation.
Narrative 1: I responded to <opponent-possessive> Facebook smear campaign against me by launching my own Facebook smear campaign against <him/her>.
Narrative 2: I ignored an ad campaign launched by <opponent> on Facebook that smeared my political views with misinformation.
Choice 3: Address the public about the ad
Narrative 3: I addressed <opponent-possessive> Facebook smear campaign by posting thousands of official replies stating the truth.
Choice 4: Call my opponent and tell <him/her> off
Narrative 4: I called <opponent> on the phone after <he/she> posted a malicious smear campaign against me on Facebook and said the polls would soon reveal that <he/she> was the real loser.

Title: Rally Crasher
Body: While making an impassioned speech at an outdoor campaign rally, you suddenly notice a massive hot air balloon floating toward the crowd that has <opponent-possessive> face painted on it with a speech bubble saying, "Vote for me, not a big baby".
Narrative 1: I ended a political rally when <opponent> floated a hot air balloon over the crowd that said I was a big baby.
Narrative 2: I laughed when <opponent> attempted to play a prank on my campaign rally by floating a hot air balloon over the crowd with <his/her> face painted on the side.
Narrative 3: I called the police on <opponent> when <he/she> attempted to play a prank on my campaign rally by floating a hot air balloon over the crowd.
Narrative 4: I told everyone at a campaign rally that <opponent> was for so desperate for votes, that <he/she> would resort to slanderous messages posted on hot air balloons.

Title: Loaded Questions
Body: While campaigning in the gorgeous state of Colorado, you receive an invitation to attend a private event held at the governor's mansion. When you arrive, the place reeks of weed, and the governor approaches you holding a joint, asking if you want a hit.
Narrative 1: I smoked weed with the governor of Colorado.
Narrative 2: I regretfully declined an opportunity to smoke weed with the governor of Colorado.
Choice 3: Slap the joint out of his hand
Narrative 3: When the governor of Colorado offered me a hit of marijuana, I got so offended that I slapped the joint out of his hand.
Narrative 4: The governor of Colorado offered me a hit of marijuana while I was at his mansion, but it made me so uncomfortable I left the party.

Title: Financial Aid
Body: Just as your campaign is starting to gain some serious momentum, your finance manager says you spent way too much on advertising, and now you're nearly out of money.
Choice 1: Ask the public for financial support
Narrative 1: After spending way too much on expensive advertising, I had to beg the public for money to keep my election ad campaign alive.
Choice 2: Work with the money I have
Narrative 2: After spending way too much on expensive advertising, I had to cut way back on everything just to keep my election campaign alive.
Narrative 3: After spending way too much on expensive advertising, I had to ask investors for money to keep my election ad campaign alive.
Narrative 4: I decided to end my ad campaign after almost completely depleting my funds.

Title: Transparency Test
Body: The last <political-office> left the citizens of your <jurisdiction> insanely wary about political corruption, and they want to know what you will do to make your leadership more transparent.
Choice 1: Let citizens look through my phone
Narrative 1: To make my leadership of the <jurisdiction> more transparent, I told voters that if I was elected, they could look through my phone whenever they wanted.
Narrative 2: To make my leadership of the <jurisdiction> more transparent, I told voters that if I were elected, I would have a weekly address of everything I'd accomplished that week.
Narrative 3: I assured the voters of my <jurisdiction> that if elected, nobody would ever need to worry about corruption while I was in office.
Narrative 4: To make my leadership of the <jurisdiction> more transparent, I told the voters that if elected, I would form a politically diverse group of advisors.

Title: Fancy That
Body: A campaign advisor is suggesting that you brush up on your traditional UK etiquette to help secure votes from an older demographic.
Narrative 1: I repeatedly practiced my royal wave in an effort to gain the support of older, more traditional voters.
Narrative 2: I repeatedly practiced my kitchen utensil table manners in an effort to gain the support of older, more traditional voters.
Narrative 3: I practiced the proper holding of a teacup after an advisor suggested I brush up on etiquette to gain the support of older voters. I learned everything I know from the Queen.
Narrative 4: To gain the support of older, more traditional voters, I memorized a litany of dry, self-deprecating jokes that I used on the campaign trail.

Title: Odd Job
Body: While looking for opportunities to get more publicity, you discover some unique events that could help you appeal to some of the more eccentric of voters.
Narrative 1: I attended the Cooper's Hill Cheese-Rolling event as a way to gain the support of some of the UK's most eccentric voters.
Narrative 2: I participated in a maypole dancing event as a way to gain the support of some of the UK's most eccentric voters.
Narrative 3: I participated in a bog snorkeling event as a way to gain the support of some of the UK's most eccentric voters.
Narrative 4: I decided not to participate in any of the UK's more eccentric events, even though I could have exposed myself to a whole new demographic of voters.

Title: Mark Your Territory
Body: While participating in a televised debate, the host asks what you will do to create a long-lasting, positive impression for the people in your state.
Narrative 1: I answered a debate question by saying that I would like to create more state parks if elected as the next governor.
Narrative 2: During a debate, I informed the audience that if I were elected as governor, I would make universities more affordable.
Narrative 3: During a debate, I informed the audience that if I were elected as governor, I would fix the correctional system.
Narrative 4: During a debate, I informed the audience that if I were elected as governor, I would provide incentives to bring more big business into our state.
Narrative 5: During a debate, I informed the audience that if I were elected as governor, I would build more mental health facilities.
Narrative 6: During a debate, I informed the audience that if I were elected as governor, I would build more drug treatment facilities.
Narrative 7: During a debate, I informed the audience that if I were elected as governor, I would end animal cruelty.
Narrative 8: During a debate, I informed the audience that if I were elected as governor, I would transition the state to renewable energy sources.
Narrative 9: During a debate, I informed the audience that if I were elected as governor, I would push hard for more nude beaches.

Title: Ground Game
Body: A political advisor says you need to up your "ground game" to get elected, and suggests you start knocking on doors to meet potential voters face to face.
Narrative 1: I knocked on 1,000 doors a day to get more face-to-face interaction with voters in my area.
Narrative 2: I knocked on 100 doors a day to get more face-to-face interaction with voters in my area.
Narrative 3: I knocked on 10 doors a day to get more face-to-face interaction with voters in my area.
Choice 4: I'm not knocking on strangers' doors
Narrative 4: I decided not to bother people by knocking on their doors, even though it would have given me more face-to-face interaction with voters in my area.

Title: Pants on Fire!
Body: While listening to <opponent-possessive> response during a debate, <he/she> makes a comment that you know is an outright lie.
Narrative 1: I waited patiently to respond after <opponent> told a blatant lie during a debate. I then corrected <his/her> false statement, citing scientific research to support my claim.
Narrative 2: I immediately interrupted <opponent> when <he/she> told a lie during a televised political debate.
Narrative 3: When <opponent> told a blatant lie during a televised debate, I erupted into a rage and called <him/her> a throttlebottom.
Choice 4: Make funny faces to show your displeasure
Narrative 4: I made ridiculous faces of disgust and frustration while listening to <opponent> make dishonest claims at a political debate.

Title: Red River Rivalry
Body: You walk onto the stage at a massive campaign rally and vigorously greet the crowd by shouting, "Helloooooooooo Oklahomaaaaaa!" You're immediately are bombarded with a cacophony of boos before remembering that you're in Texas.
Narrative 1: I apologized to the fine folk of Texas after mistakenly addressing them as Oklahomans. The boos simmered down but continued throughout my speech.
Narrative 2: I ignored it when I mistakenly addressed the fine folk of Texas as Oklahomans. It was hard for anyone to hear anything I said because of the boos.
Narrative 3: I ran off stage after mistakenly addressing the fine folk of Texas as Oklahomans. They showed their displeasure by plastering me with Texas-sized tomatoes as I fled the venue.
Narrative 4: After mistakenly addressing a crowd of Texans as Oklahomans, I played it off by saying it was my way of making sure they were paying attention.

Title: Flip-Flopper
Body: During a televised debate, <opponent> accuses you of flip-flopping your stand on gun control.
Choice 1: Arms of all types should be legal
Narrative 1: I stated at a debate that the 2nd amendment gives Americans the right to bear arms of any type, including nuclear weapons and missiles.
Narrative 2: I stated at a debate that the 2nd amendment should be repealed by an amendment that prohibits Americans from owning guns of any type.
Narrative 3: I stated at a debate that the 2nd amendment gives Americans the right to bear arms, but that not all types of guns should be legal. I added that anything as powerful as an automatic assault rifle needs to be banned.
Narrative 4: When <opponent> called me a flip-flopper on gun control during a televised debate, I answered by saying the 2nd Amendment gave Americans the right to bear arms.

Title: Balance the Budget
Body: Your campaign team tells you that voters want to know your plan for managing the budget if elected as <political-office>.
Narrative 1: I told voters that, if elected, I would increase taxes and raise spending.
Narrative 2: I told voters that, if elected, I would increase taxes and lower spending.
Narrative 3: I told voters that, if elected, I would decrease taxes and lower spending.
Narrative 4: I told voters that, if elected, I would decrease taxes and raise spending.

Title: Die-hard Fanatic
Body: While at a press conference in Boston, a reporter tells you that he's a die-hard Boston Red Sox fan and then asks what you think about the New York Yankees.
Narrative 1: I told a reporter, who identified as a die-hard Red Sox fan, that I loved the New York Yankees.
Narrative 2: I told a reporter, who happened to be a Boston Red Sox fan, that I too was a member of Red Sox Nation.
Narrative 3: I told a reporter, who identified as a die-hard Red Sox fan, that I loved both the New York Yankees and the Boston Red Sox.
Narrative 4: I told a reporter, who happened to be a Boston Red Sox fan, that I had no interest in baseball and didn't care about the Yankees or any team, for that matter.

Title: Photo-Op
Body: Various media companies are coming at you with offers to be featured in their magazine. You recognize this as a prime opportunity to get your face in front of the public and decide to accept one of the offers.
Narrative 1: I chose to be featured in 'Time' magazine as a way to get some exposure to the voters. I gained a lot of supporters around the world far and wide!
Narrative 2: I chose to be featured in 'People' magazine as a way to get some exposure to the voters. They told me they would consider me as a candidate for Sexiest Person of the Year!
Narrative 3: I chose to be featured in 'National Geographic' magazine as a way to get some exposure to the voters. It was a good opportunity for me to share my love for the natural habitats of the world!
Narrative 4: I chose to be featured in 'Psychology Today' magazine as a way to get some exposure to the voters. It was a good way for me to share my passion for health and my vision for helping those with mental health issues.
Narrative 5: I chose to be featured in 'Playboy' magazine as a way to get some exposure to the voters. The plan backfired when the media reported it was a tasteless move.
Narrative 6: I chose to be featured in 'Cosmo' magazine as a way to get some exposure to the voters. They made me look super sexy!
Narrative 7: I chose to be featured in 'Good Housekeeping' magazine as a way to get some exposure to the voters. Now the whole world knows just how domestic I can be!
Narrative 8: I chose to be featured in 'ESPN: The Magazine' as a way to get some exposure to the voters. The article made fun of my physique and lack of athleticism, so it really hurt my reputation among sports fans.
Narrative 9: I chose to be featured in 'Bloomberg Businessweek' magazine as a way to get some exposure to the voters. I gained a lot of supporters from business owners and financially savvy citizens!

Title: Pizza Lover
Body: During a televised debate held in New York City, the host asks how you expect to gain local support when <lover> is on the record stating that Chicago-style pizza is much better than New York pizza.
Narrative 1: I told a debate host that I fully support whichever pizza <lover> enjoys the most, and that it would never diminish my leadership skills.
Narrative 2: I told a debate host that even I thought <lover-possessive> pizza preferences were egregious. It got a laugh from the crowd.
Narrative 3: A debate host in New York City asked me a ridiculous question about <lover-possessive> pizza preferences, but I just dismissed it, saying we should discuss relevant matters instead.
Narrative 4: After a debate host asked me about <lover-possessive> pizza preferences, I just laughed it off. It was pretty funny.
